alignments.note: Imperative rendered by the bare English verb.

Article governing the expressed noun δεσμίων, whose phrase the ASV recasts as a finite relative clause. Rule 92: where the ASV writes a separate antecedent pronoun the article owns that pronoun, as τοὺς … ἀποστόλους → them that were does; the noun keeps the relativizer and copula.

The noun carries the supplied relativizer and copula under rule 92, the article having already taken its antecedent pronoun. No Greek preposition stands for in, so the whole phrase that are in bonds is the noun's; headed on bonds as the word realizing δέσμιος.

Participle of συνδέομαι. The with is the compound verb's own particle and no Greek preposition is expressed, so rule 36 does not divide it; the supplied object them stays with the verb that requires it in English under rule 74's contrast clause. Headed on the lexical verb word bound per rule 17.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun and nothing else, the participle keeping the relative clause.
Participle taking the relativizer and copula as rule 32 requires. Headed on the verb word treated rather than the modifier ill, as rule 91 heads βλασφημοῦντες → speaking evil of you on speaking.
Second comparative adverb rendered as, analysed exactly as s004 under rule 24.
Intensifying καί realized by also and so aligned on its own under rule 65's English-side test; no correlative οὕτως or καθώς stands here, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question.
Expressed participle of εἰμί rendered being; the clause is not verbless, so rules 53 and 62 do not arise and the preposition carries no supplied copula.
The Greek is anarthrous, so no article competes for the determiner and the supplied the is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines.

review_notes: Every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once; no unit is unrepresented or added.

The two parallel members are analysed alike under rule 24: τῶν δεσμίων has an expressed head noun so rule 92 splits antecedent pronoun from relative clause, while τῶν κακουχουμένων governs a participle so rule 32 splits pronoun from clause. Both give the article only its pronoun.
Competing reading on s003/s002: giving the whole them that are in bonds to a single article+noun unit was rejected under rules 2 and 26, the pieces being independently recoverable.

Competing reading on s005: putting with on the participle's dependence rather than the verb was considered; no Greek preposition token is expressed, so rule 36 has nothing to divide and the compound verb keeps its own particle.
